Explicate

EK-spli-kayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To explicate is to analyze in order to reveal meaning.

The study guide's central task was to explicate the poem's final image and show what it reveals about the speaker's state of mind.

Worked Example

In her essay, Maria explicated the short story's ambiguous ending, walking line by line through the clues that pointed toward the narrator's guilt.

Maria didn't just summarize the ending -- she broke it down piece by piece to reveal what it actually meant.

How Explicate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

elucidate

elucidate: to make something clear by explaining it

interpret

interpret: to explain the meaning of something

Antonyms

obscure

obscure: to make something unclear or hard to understand

How Strong Is It? — describe → explicate → dissect

describe vs. explicate

describe vs. explicate: To merely describe a poem is to say what happens in it; to explicate it is to show exactly how each part creates its meaning.

dissect vs. explicate

dissect vs. explicate: To dissect a text goes even further than explicating it, pulling apart every device so thoroughly that the poem's feeling can get lost.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of explicate.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-

prefix — ex-: out (Latin)

root — plic

root — plic: to fold (Latin (plicare))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- ('out') plus the root plic- ('to fold,' from Latin plicare) plus the verb-forming -ate paints unfolding something that was folded up -- explicating a poem means unfolding its meaning so it can finally be seen clearly.

Use the root in a new word: duplicate

Use the root in a new word: duplicate: Duplicate comes from the same 'fold' root -- literally to fold something over again, making a second copy.

Root Check

Word Choice

Explicate is a formal, academic word -- reach for it when discussing careful textual or literary analysis, not everyday explaining. It pairs naturally with 'explicate a text/poem/passage.'
